title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative Result under Shared‑Generation Semantics
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment (study_id = cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) that tested whether a deterministic verifier pipeline (generate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional repair) reduces the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe intent→configuration proposals produced by a hosted LLM on synthetic NetOps tasks. Design: N=200 preregistered unique tasks in a paired design comparing (a) baseline LLM‑only and (b) guarded pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) resulting in model_calls_used = 200 (preregistered maximum_model_calls for independent per‑arm generation = 400). Results (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0). Estimated paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Because identical per‑pair generations were produced and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis (that a verifier reduces unsafe proposals) was not testable in this execution. We publish the complete preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of testability failure, and give concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation, adversarial injection budgeting, exploratory ROC reserve) for informative repeats. Key archived artifacts cited in text include execution/model_configuration.json, execution/execution_manifest.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, and execution/scoring/*.json.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises productivity gains for network operations (NetOps) but creates operational safety risks: an incorrect or ill‑timed change can break reachability, violate policy, or cause outages. Prior proposals therefore combine LLMs with deterministic validators, sandboxed simulators, and generate–validate–repair pipelines to reduce hallucination‑driven errors and enforce workflow constraints. To move beyond small prototypes and design claims we preregistered and executed a workflow‑centred, confirmatory paired experiment to quantify whether deterministic verifier augmentation reduces verifier‑detected unsafe proposals under both benign and adversarial prompts.

Research question. The preregistered primary question (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) asked: How does deterministic tool‑augmentation (generate → deterministic validator → optional repair) change the rate of unsafe network‑change proposals produced by a hosted LLM under benign and adversarial NetOps prompts? The primary estimand was the paired SAFE‑rate difference: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, evaluated with an exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Contributions. (1) A reproducible, fully archived preregistered paired experiment and deterministic artifacts for N=200 intent→configuration tasks (execution/*, analysis/*). (2) An artifact‑grounded diagnosis of a ceiling/testability failure that rendered the preregistered contrast non‑informative in this run. (3) Concrete, artifact‑supported design mitigations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial injection to target nonzero baseline unsafe rates, and exploratory ROC estimation) for informative repeats. We emphasize that this run does not provide evidence of verifier inefficacy; it documents how execution semantics and budgeting choices interacted with the estimand to make the test uninformative.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and prototype reports document broad interest in LLMs for NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, remediation) and the use of tool‑augmentation and verification to improve correctness [arXiv:2605.12729; SSRN:7132138; IEEE OJCOMS 2026]. Generate–validate–repair and divide–verify–refine pipelines have been empirically shown to reduce constraint violations in selected settings, though effect sizes vary with verifier fidelity and prompt design [openalex:W4412888330; openalex:W7161354925]. Red‑teaming and guardrail literatures emphasize trade‑offs between false refusals and missed unsafe proposals and recommend workflow‑centred, replayable evaluations that archive model outputs and deterministic validator traces [TechRxiv:177004277; TechRxiv:177006109].

Positioning. Unlike prior prototype evaluations that report improvements on curated case sets, our contribution is methodological and reproducible: we publish a confirmatory preregistered run with deterministic artifacts and analyze how generation semantics (shared vs independent candidate draws), model‑call budgeting, and adversarial strength determine the testability of a paired causal contrast.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as cand-2026-01-prereg-v1. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (SAFE encoded 1). The design: paired binary comparison with N=200 unique tasks; primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided via paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10000 resamples (seed = 1729). The preregistration included power planning that assumed a baseline unsafe rate ≈10–15% and a detectable paired reduction of ≈7 percentage points (discordant proportions p10≈0.07, p01≈0.01, yielding n≈174 for 80% power), and it reserved up to 50 exploratory tasks for ROC estimation.

Task generation and sampling. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks under a preregistered RNG schedule (master seed = 42, per‑task seeds 1..200). Tasks target operationally meaningful changes restricted to admin/mtu/vlan fields across multi‑device, single‑AS topologies; each task manifest entry records constraints, required sequences, and expected final state (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl). The preregistration split tasks into benign and adversarial clusters; adversarial prompts used templated obfuscation and negation transforms intended to raise baseline unsafe rates.

Pipelines, validator, and repairs. Two pipelines were compared: baseline (LLM only) and guarded (LLM candidate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional single repair). deterministic_netops_validator_v5 runs a deterministic sandbox validation applying full_intent_constraint_validation; scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) contain both validation_before and validation_after traces, violation lists, and a binary SAFE/UNSAFE label used by the analysis executor. For the confirmatory episodes no automatic repairs were applied (repair_provider_trace = null in scoring artifacts); remediation behavior was reserved for exploratory protocol variants.

Generation semantics and model accounting. The preregistration permitted either independent per‑arm generation (two independent LLM calls per pair) or shared_initial_candidate (one LLM call per pair shared across arms). The executed run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json. As a result model_calls_used = 200 (one per paired task) rather than the preregistered maximum_model_calls = 400 for independent draws; this exact accounting is archived in execution/execution_manifest.json and is central to the testability diagnosis.

Analysis and missingness handling. The primary analysis was deterministic: paired_binary_analysis_v1 produced the 2×2 contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00), an exact McNemar two‑sided p‑value, and the paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples). Preregistered missingness rules allowed one retry for failed model calls and automatic replacement of contaminated tasks; abort/downgrade rules applied if technical failures exceeded 10% of pairs. Execution produced zero technical failures or exclusions; the deterministic_reconciliation.json and analysis/missingness_summary.csv confirm complete_pair_count = 200.

Reproducibility posture. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced here are archived in the supplied bundle (notably execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/execution_manifest.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, and execution/scoring/*.json). These artifacts permit deterministic replay of the confirmatory episodes and reexecution of the paired_binary_analysis_v1 analysis with the stated seeds.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The harness completed planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 arm scorings derived from a single shared initial generation per task) with failed_episode_count = 0 and model_calls_used = 200 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Provider audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json records hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false (shared semantics implemented via a single shared_initial_generation per pair).

Primary outcomes. Analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline SAFE successes = 200/200 and guarded SAFE successes = 200/200 (SAFE encoded as 1). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). These figures are reproduced verbatim from analysis/results.json and the CSV artifacts.

Representative diagnostics. Scoring JSON examples (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate content across baseline and guarded arms and validator traces with violation_count = 0 in both validation_before and validation_after blocks; repair_provider_trace entries are null for confirmatory episodes. The deterministic_reconciliation.json artifact confirms consistent episode accounting (complete_pair_count = 200; n_11 = 200) and that all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Interpretation. The observed data contain no discordant pairs (n10, n01 = 0) because (a) shared generation semantics made both arms receive identical LLM candidates, and (b) those shared candidates passed the validator, so baseline produced zero detected unsafe proposals. Under these conditions the preregistered paired contrast has no power to estimate a verifier effect—the data provide a reproducible ceiling/testability failure rather than evidence for or against verifier efficacy.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded diagnosis of a non‑informative confirmatory test. Three archive‑verifiable facts combined to produce the ceiling/testability failure in this execution: (1) shared initial generation: independent_condition_generation = false (execution/model_configuration.json) produced a single LLM candidate reused by both arms (execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt); (2) zero baseline unsafe rate: baseline SAFE = 200/200 (analysis/condition_summary.csv); (3) budgeting choice: executing shared generation used model_calls_used = 200 instead of the preregistered 400 for independent draws (execution/execution_manifest.json). When the same candidate is SAFE under the validator and no repairs are applied, discordance is impossible and the paired test is uninformative.

Design implications and concrete mitigations. Because the preregistered estimand requires per‑arm variability, independent per‑arm generation should be the default for paired causal contrasts; for N=200 tasks that change increases the model call budget by exactly 200 calls (executed 200 vs preregistered maximum 400). If budget constraints exist, prioritize independent draws over increasing the number of models sampled—paired contrasts need per‑arm variability to be testable. To achieve the power assumptions of the preregistration (baseline unsafe ≈10–15% and detectable paired reduction ≈7 percentage points), preregister and inject stronger adversarial transforms or set an adversarial injection fraction to ensure nonzero baseline unsafe rates under the target model. Finally, use the exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) prior to confirmatory testing to estimate verifier ROC and refusal trade‑offs and to calibrate adversarial strength; these exploratory ROC estimates are part of the preregistered plan.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the key internal threat here is choice of generation semantics (shared vs independent) which deterministically removed per‑arm variability; this is an execution choice recorded in model_configuration.json rather than a post hoc change. Construct validity: the binary SAFE/UNSAFE label derives from deterministic_netops_validator_v5 running in a synthetic sandbox (execution/scoring/*.json); validator completeness against real production failure modes is limited. External validity: tasks are synthetic single‑AS topologies generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; generalization to multi‑AS, vendor‑specific, or live telemetry contexts is untested. Conclusion validity: sample size and power planning were preregistered assuming nonzero baseline unsafe rates; the realized baseline rate = 0% invalidated the planned power assumptions and rendered the primary hypothesis non‑testable.

Operational implications. Practitioners evaluating verifier augmentation in NetOps pipelines should explicitly record generation semantics and model‑call accounting in preregistrations; a published run that reports only the number of tasks without model‑call breakdowns can conceal testability failures. When budgets force shared generation, researchers should use the run as a diagnostic (as here) rather than an efficacy claim. When the objective is causal inference on verifier effect, allocate the extra model calls required for independent per‑arm draws or use an alternative estimand suited to shared draws (e.g., pre/post repair outcomes with injected unsafe candidates).
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully archived, preregistered paired experiment comparing an LLM baseline and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and for the declared model (gpt-5-mini), both arms produced zero verifier‑detected unsafe proposals (paired difference = 0.0; p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Because identical per‑pair generations were produced and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis could not be meaningfully evaluated. The scientific contribution is methodological and reproducible: (1) we publish a complete preregistered run with deterministic artifacts that permit exact replay; (2) we provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why this execution was non‑informative for verifier efficacy; and (3) we provide concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation, adversarial budgeting to target baseline unsafe rates ≈10–15%, and exploratory ROC estimation) for informative repeats. All execution and analysis artifacts cited here are archived in the supplied bundle (execution/*, analysis/*) to support deterministic replays and community replication.

limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt‑5‑mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or explicit injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
